page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-8 is an Arm64-based virtual machine instance belonging to the c4a server family. It is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by the Ampere Neoverse-V2 processor architecture, featuring 8 physical cores with 1 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 64 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and features no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong memory performance, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaches 200.21 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also demonstrate strong performance at 32.23 GB/sec and 14.36 GB/sec respectively. However, cryptographic operations show relative weakness, with the Passmark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 25% at 1675.45. Other metrics, including stress-ng CPU performance, Redis SET operations at 17.59 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 21.74 GB/sec, fall within the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4a-highmem-8 offers a high-density memory configuration on an energy-efficient Arm64 architecture, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. Given its high memory-to-core ratio and strong memory bandwidth, this instance is well-suited for in-memory databases, caching layers such as Redis, data processing tasks, and lightweight language model inference.
